title: Opening gameplay and completing a random quest, all code is Opus5.5
author: thewendigoo
selftext:
I'm sorry about the mouse on the recording lmao.

The art and music is made by me, but I did not write a single line of code for this. In fact, I have no idea how to. Some of the sound design is mine as well (guns), but some of it I just asked Claude to find free sound asset packs and use them. Otherwise it would just generate them. Kind of a sneaky way around using AI, while ABSOLUTELY using AI. Since I'm still a certified hypocrite AI hater. I'm coming around though alright, chill. 

I keep getting carried away breaking things and then having to go back and do a bunch of iteration to get things looking right, so still a lot of broken stuff at the moment, but if you just keep bashing your head against Claude it gets worked out eventually. 

Game already has a full map editor and the ability to import new art and add items/walls/floors/mobs/data pertaining to them. I plan on adding a quest designer, and some other stuff. Essentially having a highly user friendly modding engine thing built into the game itself. So that if I lose access to the ol LLM's I can still work on the game. So far this has worked which I find more insane than just making the game. Its also alleviated my dependency on Claude to add new things. Which is nice because that shit expensive dog. 

Spent a lot of time being a big sad boy about AI as an artist and musician, but god damn if this hasn't healed me.

Building cut aways are currently a bit broken because I added multilevel buildings/basements, and that caused a lot of chaos. Just haven't got around to berating Claude about it yet. Only problem I have is that there is a seemingly endless amount of iteration required to actually get to where you want to be, but still it's way easier than actually doing the shit. 

Also, there is a black outline shader that I like the look of, but with the fog effect it washes everything out. Granted. That's what fog does. If someone can tell me what to say to Mr. computer to fix it lmk. Looks fine without it as well, but it adds a little sauce that I dont want to give up on.

comments.author: StarsSpawn
comments.body:
Good art, I could tell it wasn't made by AI immediately. I like the hand drawn/paper/flat aesthetic, have not seen that in any game, what were your inspirations? Also you can hide the mouse in games by asking the ai to add mouse lock to the game, just make sure you can also unlock/lock the mouse by pressing a key on the keyboard. 

  
Some things I think you can add: 1. More character poses. The 2d art with the characters text in a box at the bottom reminds me of visual novels. When characters are talking you can make them animated by hand drawing more art of them in different poses that relates to what they are saying, or you can do the lazy way and just make them shake or rotate back and forth, idk. 2. Add windows to the buildings so it's not too dark and players can see inside. Or make the player emit a faint glow or disable/hide shadows in building. 3. Draw more art and flip environmental objects like rocks, trees, shrubs for variation. Add transition tiles for the ground, buildings, whatever.

  
Thx for reading, you don't have to add anything you don't want though, it's still a ton of work to make a game even if you are using AI to code.

replies.author: thewendigoo
replies.body:
Thank you! Good ideas, lots of things on the list. Environmental objects do currently flip. I was also thinking of adding an animal crossing style voice to characters with some movement. There's also suppose to be a flashlight in dark interiors, but that's all a little broken at the moment. 

The design is kind of just rimworld pawns, with more drawing.

Weirdly the paper style just happened because the game started as a 2D traditional roguelike survival crafting game. I then later had it converted into realtime combat and 3D. I needed a way to stand up the drawings. A bit of Paper Mario maybe.

There is a ton of weird stuff happening under the hood that isn't visible in this, but a lot of mechanics I don't have art for are being hidden right now or you'd see a lot of ASCII laying around.
